text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Frederick Chiluba says the government will not entertain opposition calls for fresh elections because he was legitimately elected.
- Finance minister Ronald Penza says some opposition parties and other local groups tried to frustrate government efforts at the recent Consultative Group meeting with protest notes to donors.
- President Frederick Chiluba admits that the present economic state has subjected many Zambians to poverty, but blames the former government for the state of affairs.
- President Frederick Chiluba defends public servants threatening to go on strike, saying their cause is justified.
- Over 200 workers at the state-run Zambia State Insurance Corp stage a sit-in to push for a 7.5 percent pay rise.
